[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#purpose-statement]

### Purpose Statement

This standard defines the mandatory label taxonomy for all AI agent dispatch pipelines operating against issue tracker work items. It specifies which labels exist, what each label means, who may apply them, and under what conditions. Consistent label taxonomy is the mechanism by which intent signals are reliably translated into agent pipeline routing decisions — without it, teams create ad-hoc labels that overlap, conflict, or fail silently when they do not match the pipeline's expected trigger conditions.
page_texts.5:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#scope]

### Scope

**In scope:**
- All labels used to trigger, route, or track the status of AI agent pipeline execution in the issue tracker
- The conditions under which each label may be applied
- The process for extending the taxonomy with new labels

**Out of scope:**
- Labels used exclusively for human workflow management (e.g., `bug`, `enhancement`, `priority:high`) that are not consumed by agent pipelines
- Internal labels applied by agents to their own produced artifacts (e.g., labels applied to agent-produced PRs)
- Labeling conventions for repositories that do not operate agent dispatch pipelines
page_texts.6:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

**Mandatory.** All repositories operating an AI agent dispatch pipeline MUST use this taxonomy exclusively for agent pipeline control. Teams MUST NOT create custom labels that duplicate, extend, or partially implement these functions outside of the extension process defined in this standard.
page_texts.7:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#business-rationale]

### Business Rationale

A label is the execution trigger in the agent dispatch model. A label applied to an issue fires a webhook event that initiates the agent pipeline. If multiple label conventions exist across teams — some using `ai-task`, others `agent-task`, others `copilot-run` — the agent pipeline infrastructure cannot be shared, pipeline monitoring cannot be centralized, and compliance auditing cannot consistently identify all agent-executed work. A single taxonomy makes the agent execution queue auditable, portable, and operable at organization scale.

---
page_texts.9:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

**REQ-001 — Mandatory Taxonomy Adoption**: Every repository operating an AI agent dispatch pipeline MUST create all labels defined in this standard's taxonomy before enabling the pipeline. The labels MUST be created with the exact names and color conventions specified in the Technical Specifications.

**REQ-002 — Exclusive Execution Trigger**: The `agent-task` label and only the `agent-task` label MUST be used as the execution trigger for the agent dispatch pipeline. No other label, webhook event, or schedule-based trigger MUST be used as a substitute or addition to `agent-task` for initiating agent dispatch.

**REQ-003 — Routing Label Requirement**: Every `agent-task`-labeled issue MUST also carry exactly one routing label from the approved routing label set (`agent:implementation`, `agent:documentation`, `agent:testing`, `agent:infrastructure`, `agent:ui`). The dispatch pipeline MUST validate the presence of exactly one routing label before invoking any agent and MUST halt with a corrective comment if zero or more than one routing label is present.

**REQ-004 — Application Authority**: The `agent-task` label MUST only be applied by a human who has reviewed the spec for compliance with STD-GOV-AI-001. The label application is the formal approval signal that the spec is ready for execution. Automated tools and bots MUST NOT apply `agent-task` to issues without human authorization.

**REQ-005 — Status Label Management**: Status labels (`agent:complete`, `agent:blocked`) MUST only be applied by the agent dispatch pipeline itself — never manually by engineers. Manual application of status labels creates false status signals that compromise pipeline monitoring and audit trail integrity.

**REQ-006 — Taxonomy Extension Control**: New labels for agent pipeline use MUST be proposed via a formal request to the Enterprise Architecture Practice and approved before deployment. Teams MUST NOT deploy custom agent routing labels that are not in the approved taxonomy.
page_texts.10:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

- **REP-001**: Apply the routing label at the same time the spec is authored, not at the time the `agent-task` trigger label is applied — this makes the review easier because the intended agent type is visible during spec peer review
- **REP-002**: Configure repository label protection (where the platform supports it) to prevent unauthorized removal of status labels applied by the pipeline
- **REP-003**: When a task spans multiple agent types (e.g., implementation followed by documentation), create separate issues for each agent type rather than applying multiple routing labels to one issue
- **REP-004**: Use the `agent:blocked` label as an active signal in sprint review — blocked issues should be triaged, not silently left in the backlog
page_texts.11:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- **PRO-001**: MUST NOT create labels that partially duplicate taxonomy function (e.g., `ai-task`, `copilot-task`, `bot-task`, `auto-implement`) in repositories operating the standard agent pipeline
- **PRO-002**: MUST NOT apply `agent-task` to an issue that has not been validated for spec compliance with STD-GOV-AI-001 — the trigger label is an approval, not a request
- **PRO-003**: MUST NOT apply multiple routing labels to a single issue — one issue, one agent type
- **PRO-004**: MUST NOT manually apply or remove `agent:complete` or `agent:blocked` — these are pipeline-managed status signals
- **PRO-005**: MUST NOT use `agent-task` as a general-purpose "this needs AI assistance" marker for human-assisted tasks — the label has a specific, machine-consequential meaning in the dispatch pipeline
page_texts.12:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#exceptions-process]

### Exceptions Process

1. A team requiring a new routing label (e.g., `agent:data-migration` for a specialized agent configuration) submits a label extension request to EA Practice with: the proposed label name, description, color, the agent configuration it routes to, and evidence that no existing routing label serves the need
2. EA Practice reviews within 5 business days; approved labels are added to this standard in the next version
3. A team may NOT deploy a proposed new label until it appears in an approved version of this standard — even if approval is expected

page_texts.15:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#canonical-label-definitions]

#### Canonical Label Definitions

All labels MUST be created with the exact names in the following table. Color codes are provided as defaults; teams may adjust colors for accessibility or platform theming while preserving the name convention.

| Label | Category | Applied By | Default Color | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent-task` | Execution Trigger | Human only (post-review) | `#0075CA` (blue) | Triggers the agent dispatch pipeline. Applied only after spec has been peer-reviewed for STD-GOV-AI-001 compliance. |
| `agent:implementation` | Routing | Human | `#2EA44F` (green) | Routes to the code implementation agent configuration. |
| `agent:documentation` | Routing | Human | `#2EA44F` (green) | Routes to the documentation generation agent configuration. |
| `agent:testing` | Routing | Human | `#2EA44F` (green) | Routes to the test generation agent configuration. |
| `agent:infrastructure` | Routing | Human | `#2EA44F` (green) | Routes to the infrastructure provisioning agent configuration. |
| `agent:ui` | Routing | Human | `#2EA44F` (green) | Routes to the UI implementation agent configuration (Presentation-layer / `@UI` features, per GUID-GOV-PROC-014). One `agent:ui` issue per screen. |
| `agent:complete` | Status | Pipeline only | `#6F42C1` (purple) | Applied by pipeline when agent has produced a PR and reported results. Awaiting human review. |
| `agent:blocked` | Status | Pipeline only | `#D73A4A` (red) | Applied by pipeline when execution failed at any stage. Issue requires human attention. |
| `agent:duplicate` | Status | Pipeline only | `#CFD3D7` (grey) | Applied by the pre-dispatch idempotency gate (STD-GOV-AI-004) when the incoming work item's deliverable stable-ID has already shipped under a canonical sibling. Accompanied by a `superseded by #<canonical>` comment and closure as not-planned. |
page_texts.16:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#label-mutual-exclusion-rules]

#### Label Mutual Exclusion Rules

The pipeline MUST enforce the following mutual exclusion rules, validated before agent invocation:

| Rule | Description | Pipeline Response on Violation |
|---|---|---|
| EXCL-001 | Exactly one routing label must be present when `agent-task` is present | Halt; post comment listing available routing labels; do not remove `agent-task` |
| EXCL-002 | `agent:complete` and `agent:blocked` must not both be present | Remove `agent:blocked`; apply `agent:complete` if dispatch succeeded; log anomaly |
| EXCL-003 | `agent:complete` must not be present when `agent-task` is newly applied | Remove `agent:complete` before re-triggering; log as re-execution |
page_texts.17:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#label-lifecycle-state-machine]

#### Label Lifecycle State Machine

```
[Issue created]
      │
      │ Author applies routing label (agent:implementation etc.)
      ▼
[Spec authored — routing label present, agent-task NOT yet present]
      │
      │ Peer review confirms STD-GOV-AI-001 compliance
      │ Reviewer applies agent-task
      ▼
[Queued — agent-task + routing label present]
      │
      │ Pipeline webhook fires
      ▼
[Validating — pipeline Stage 1 running]
      │
      ├─ Validation FAIL ──► [agent-task removed by pipeline] ──► [Needs Attention]
      │                       Pipeline posts corrective comment
      │
      └─ Validation PASS ──► [Dispatching — pipeline Stage 2 running]
                                    │
                                    ├─ Dispatch FAIL ──► [agent:blocked applied]
                                    │
                                    └─ Dispatch PASS ──► [agent:complete applied]
                                                          PR created (Stage 3)
```
page_texts.18:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#routing-label-to-agent-configuration-mapping]

#### Routing Label to Agent Configuration Mapping

The dispatch pipeline MUST maintain a configuration mapping from routing labels to agent configurations. This mapping MUST be version-controlled and MUST NOT be embedded as pipeline platform UI configuration.

```yaml
# Agent routing configuration — version controlled
agent_routing:
  "agent:implementation":
    agent_config: "configs/agents/implementation-agent.yaml"
    context_files:
      - ".github/copilot-instructions.md"
      - "standards/application/api-standards.md"
    max_runtime_seconds: 300
  "agent:documentation":
    agent_config: "configs/agents/documentation-agent.yaml"
    context_files:
      - ".github/copilot-instructions.md"
      - "standards/technology/markdown/"
    max_runtime_seconds: 180
  "agent:testing":
    agent_config: "configs/agents/testing-agent.yaml"
    context_files:
      - ".github/copilot-instructions.md"
    max_runtime_seconds: 240
  "agent:infrastructure":
    agent_config: "configs/agents/infrastructure-agent.yaml"
    context_files:
      - ".github/copilot-instructions.md"
      - "iac/"
    max_runtime_seconds: 300
```
page_texts.19:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#architecture-constraints]

### Architecture Constraints

- Label names MUST be lowercase with hyphens and colons as the only non-alphanumeric characters — no spaces, underscores, or uppercase letters
- The colon (`:`) in routing and status labels is a deliberate namespace separator — it visually distinguishes agent pipeline labels from general-purpose labels in the issue tracker UI
- The taxonomy MUST be documented in a machine-readable format (YAML or JSON) in the repository, not only in this standard, so that the dispatch pipeline can validate against the authoritative taxonomy definition at runtime
page_texts.21:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#machine-readable-taxonomy-definition]

#### Machine-Readable Taxonomy Definition

Teams MUST maintain the label taxonomy in a version-controlled configuration file at `.github/agent-labels.yml` (or platform equivalent):

```yaml
# .github/agent-labels.yml — authoritative label taxonomy definition
# Managed per STD-GOV-AI-002. Do not modify without EA Practice approval.
version: "1.0.0"
standard_ref: "STD-GOV-AI-002"

labels:
  trigger:
    - name: "agent-task"
      color: "0075CA"
      description: "Triggers AI agent dispatch pipeline. Apply only after spec peer review (STD-GOV-AI-001)."

  routing:
    - name: "agent:implementation"
      color: "2EA44F"
      description: "Route to code implementation agent."
    - name: "agent:documentation"
      color: "2EA44F"
      description: "Route to documentation generation agent."
    - name: "agent:testing"
      color: "2EA44F"
      description: "Route to test generation agent."
    - name: "agent:infrastructure"
      color: "2EA44F"
      description: "Route to infrastructure provisioning agent."

  status:
    - name: "agent:complete"
      color: "6F42C1"
      description: "Pipeline managed. Agent produced PR. Awaiting human review."
    - name: "agent:blocked"
      color: "D73A4A"
      description: "Pipeline managed. Agent execution failed. Requires human attention."
```

page_texts.24:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#phase-1-label-creation]

#### Phase 1: Label Creation

1. Deploy all taxonomy labels to the repository using the canonical names and default colors defined in the Technical Specifications
2. Deploy the `.github/agent-labels.yml` machine-readable taxonomy file
3. Configure branch protection or repository settings (where supported) to prevent unauthorized label deletion
4. Document the label taxonomy in the repository's agent pipeline runbook
page_texts.25:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#phase-2-pipeline-configuration]

#### Phase 2: Pipeline Configuration

1. Configure the pipeline trigger to fire on `issues.labeled` events where the label name equals `agent-task` exactly
2. Implement routing label validation as part of the validation gate (Stage 1 of PTN-TEC-AI-002): confirm exactly one routing label from the approved set is present
3. Configure the pipeline to apply `agent:complete` on successful PR creation and `agent:blocked` on any pipeline failure
4. Configure the pipeline to remove `agent-task` on validation failure (to prevent re-trigger loops) and post a corrective comment
page_texts.26:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#phase-3-governance-wiring]

#### Phase 3: Governance Wiring

1. Verify that the mutual exclusion rules (EXCL-001, EXCL-002, EXCL-003) are implemented in the validation stage
2. Add a label drift detection check to the repository's CI pipeline that compares deployed labels against `.github/agent-labels.yml` and alerts on divergence
3. Document the application authority rules (REQ-004, REQ-005) in the team's Definition of Ready
page_texts.27:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#validation-criteria]

### Validation Criteria

| Validation Area | Criteria | Verification Method | Evidence Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| All taxonomy labels deployed | All 7 labels exist with exact names | List repository labels | Label list export |
| Trigger exclusivity | No non-standard trigger labels present | Search issue history for agent executions | Pipeline execution log |
| Routing validation active | Pipeline halts when zero or >1 routing label present | Test with 0 routing labels, then 2 routing labels | Pipeline run logs for each test |
| Status label protection | `agent:complete` and `agent:blocked` not manually applicable | Attempt manual application; confirm it is logged/rejected | Access control or audit log |
| Taxonomy file present | `.github/agent-labels.yml` exists and matches deployed labels | File comparison against deployed labels | File contents + label list |
page_texts.28:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#testing-requirements]

### Testing Requirements

- **Label Trigger Test**: Confirm that applying `agent-task` without a routing label halts the pipeline with the correct comment
- **Routing Test**: Confirm that each routing label (`agent:implementation`, `agent:documentation`, `agent:testing`, `agent:infrastructure`) routes to the correct agent configuration
- **Multi-Routing Test**: Confirm that applying two routing labels halts the pipeline with a "multiple routing labels" corrective comment
- **Status Label Test**: Confirm that the pipeline applies `agent:complete` on success and `agent:blocked` on failure, and that these labels are present in the issue after the pipeline run
- **Taxonomy Drift Test**: Modify a label name in the repository and confirm the drift detection alert fires
page_texts.29:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#documentation-requirements]

### Documentation Requirements

- The label taxonomy MUST be visible in the repository's README or agent pipeline runbook with the application authority rules for each label
- The `.github/agent-labels.yml` file MUST include the `standard_ref: "STD-GOV-AI-002"` field linking it to this standard
- Any team that extends the taxonomy with an EA-Practice-approved new routing label MUST update `.github/agent-labels.yml` before deploying the new label

---
page_texts.32:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#assessment-criteria]

#### Assessment Criteria

- All 7 canonical labels deployed with exact names
- No non-standard agent pipeline labels present in the repository
- `agent-task` is never the only label on an issue that successfully triggered agent dispatch (routing label was always present)
- `agent:complete` and `agent:blocked` applied exclusively by the pipeline (no manual application in audit log)
- `.github/agent-labels.yml` present, current, and matching deployed labels
page_texts.33:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#assessment-process]

#### Assessment Process

1. Quarterly automated compliance check: CI job compares deployed labels against `.github/agent-labels.yml` and reports divergence
2. Annual standard review by EA Practice to assess whether the routing label set remains appropriate for the organization's agent types
3. Incident-triggered review whenever a pipeline fires on an unexpected label or fails to fire on `agent-task`
page_texts.34:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#monitoring-requirements]

### Monitoring Requirements

- **Label Application Audit**: Log every application of `agent-task` with the applying user's identity — this is the application authority audit trail for REQ-004
- **Routing Distribution**: Track which routing label is most used each sprint — a heavily skewed distribution may indicate that the taxonomy needs expansion or that agents are being over-used for a single delivery type
- **Blocked Rate**: Track the rate of `agent:blocked` label application — a rising blocked rate indicates agent pipeline reliability issues requiring investigation
- **Taxonomy Drift Alerts**: Alert on any divergence between deployed labels and the `.github/agent-labels.yml` taxonomy file
page_texts.36:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#exception-categories]

#### Exception Categories

- **New Routing Label**: A team needs an agent type not covered by the four approved routing labels. Requires formal extension request to EA Practice.
- **Legacy Label Migration**: A team has existing labels (`ai-task`, `copilot-run`, etc.) from prior ad-hoc agent usage. Approved for a maximum two-sprint migration window; old labels must be renamed or deleted before the window closes.
page_texts.37:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#exception-management-process]

#### Exception Management Process

1. Submit extension or migration request to EA Practice with justification
2. EA Practice approves or denies within 5 business days
3. Approved extensions are reflected in the next standard version release; teams must not deploy until the version is published
page_texts.38:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#governance-oversight]

### Governance Oversight

- **Standards Owner**: Enterprise Architecture Practice — maintains taxonomy, approves extensions, publishes version updates
- **Compliance Monitor**: Engineering Lead — ensures no non-standard labels are deployed in repositories they own
- **Governance Body**: Architecture Review Board — approves major taxonomy expansions or breaking changes
- **Subject Matter Experts**: Platform Engineering Team — advises on routing label technical implications

page_texts.41:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#example-1-standard-sprint-delivery-flow]

#### Example 1: Standard Sprint Delivery Flow

**Context:** A product engineer creates an agent task for API documentation generation.

**Label application sequence:**
1. Engineer creates issue using the agent-task template (per STD-GOV-AI-001)
2. Engineer applies `agent:documentation` during authoring (routing intent is clear from the start)
3. Peer reviewer reviews spec for STD-GOV-AI-001 compliance and confirms it meets all four requirements
4. Peer reviewer applies `agent-task` — this fires the pipeline
5. Pipeline validates spec → passes → routes to documentation agent configuration
6. Agent produces PR → pipeline applies `agent:complete` → posts success comment

**Labels on issue after completion:** `agent:documentation`, `agent:complete`
(`agent-task` removed by pipeline on completion to prevent re-trigger)
page_texts.42:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#example-2-validation-failure--missing-routing-label]

#### Example 2: Validation Failure — Missing Routing Label

**Context:** Engineer applies only `agent-task` without a routing label.

**Pipeline response:**
```
⚠️ Agent Dispatch Incomplete — No Routing Label

The `agent-task` label was applied but no agent routing label was found.
Please apply exactly one of the following labels before re-triggering:

  • `agent:implementation` — code changes
  • `agent:documentation` — documentation generation
  • `agent:testing` — test generation
  • `agent:infrastructure` — infrastructure provisioning

`agent-task` has been removed. Re-apply it after adding a routing label.
```

**Labels on issue after failure:** *(agent-task removed; routing label not yet applied — issue is in draft state)*
page_texts.43:
[standards/governance/ai-development/STD-GOV-AI-002-agent-pipeline-label-taxonomy-standard.md#example-3-taxonomy-extension-request]

#### Example 3: Taxonomy Extension Request

**Context:** A data engineering team needs an `agent:data-migration` label to route to a specialized schema migration agent.

**Extension request submitted to EA Practice:**
- Proposed label: `agent:data-migration`
- Color: `2EA44F` (consistent with routing label family)
- Description: "Route to schema migration and data transformation agent."
- Agent configuration: `configs/agents/data-migration-agent.yaml`
- Justification: Existing routing labels do not cover SQL schema migration tasks; the migration agent has specialized context requirements (database standards, migration runbook templates) that differ materially from the `agent:infrastructure` agent
- Evidence: Three teams have independently created non-standard labels for this use case in the past two sprints
